text:
The house of Yves Tanguy

where one enters only at night


With the storm-lamp


Outside, the transparent country

A diviner in his element


With the storm-lamp

With the sawmill so industrious that it can no longer be seen


And the printed fabric of the sky

—Bring the supernatural down to earth


With the storm-lamp

With the sawmill so industrious that it can no longer be seen

With all the stars of hell


Made of loops and jambs

Crab-colored in the surf


With the storm-lamp

With the sawmill so industrious that it can no longer be seen

With all the stars of hell

With the delirious streetcars held back only by their cables


Space chained, time diminished

Ariana in her little chest-room


With the storm-lamp

With the sawmill so industrious that it can no longer be seen

With all the stars of hell

With the delirious streetcars held back only by their cables

With the argonaut's endless manes


The service is run by moths

who cover their eyes with cloth


With the storm-lamp

With the sawmill so industrious that it can no longer be seen

With all the stars of hell

With the delirious streetcars held back only by their cables

With the argonaut's endless manes

With the desert's blazing furniture


There one kills, there one heals

And conspires without concealment


With the storm-lamp

With the sawmill so industrious that it can no longer be seen

With all the stars of hell

With the delirious streetcars held back only by their cables

With the argonaut's endless manes

With the desert's blazing furniture

With the signals lovers exchange from afar


That is the house of Yves Tanguy.

translation.title: Yves Tanguy’s House
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the cumulative refrain and the surreal house inventory; “lámpara-tempestad” is rendered as “storm-lamp.”
